carriedForwardChecks.scope: Previously executed for byte-identical backend/codec and native implementations; not rerun after the image-only change.

endurance.scope: Passed before the final image-identity optimization; not represented as a final-tree endurance rerun.

decisions.javascript: Keep editor/history/UI and WebGPU ownership; reduce duplicate work and use existing worker boundaries.
decisions.python: Keep compatibility codecs with bounded admission/cooperative cancellation and optimized fingerprints.
decisions.cpp: Keep existing scanner/media integration; no native source changes.
decisions.rust: No measured new migration justified in this pass.
decisions.compactExport: Reject measured prototype: lower byte count did not offset encoding/decoding and peak-memory cost.
decisions.additionalWorkers: Do not move cold GPU/copy/driver work across an unmeasured scene boundary.

limits: No release or publishing; implementation remains on the isolated local branch.
Windows/NVIDIA evidence does not certify macOS/Linux, installers, arbitrary projects or every driver.
Resource allowances are estimates, not whole-process/driver hard limits. Sparse-edit growth is reassessed only at full snapshots.
Cold tick 1703 and large first-source export validation remain expensive. No blanket responsiveness or zero-regression guarantee.
Future native/transport/worker changes require new end-to-end evidence and exact semantic compatibility.
